verifications.claim: Google has agreed to a $135 million class-action settlement regarding allegations that Android devices transmitted data to Google using cellular data without user permission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Google agreed to a $135 million class action settlement to resolve claims that it used Android devices to transfer information to Google without user permission, consuming cellular data.' R2: 'Google... agreed to settle the case for $135 million... Android devices to send information back to its servers without user permission.'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly state the $135M settlement for claims of unauthorized cellular data transmission from Android devices to Google.

verifications.claim: U.S. residents who used an Android device on a cellular network since Nov. 12, 2017, may qualify for a payment.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'benefits consumers who have used mobile devices running the Android operating system to access the internet through cellular data networks since Nov. 12, 2017.' R2: 'used an Android device with a cellular data plan... from Nov. 12, 2017.'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm eligibility for U.S. Android users accessing internet via cellular data/networks since Nov. 12, 2017.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Google has not admitted any wrongdoing but agreed to a $135 million class action settlement.' R3: 'Google denied that it did anything wrong but agreed to settle the lawsuit.'
verifications.reasoning: Every reference explicitly states Google denied wrongdoing or did not admit fault.

verifications.claim: U.S. residents who used an Android device with a cellular data plan to access the internet between Nov. 12, 2017, and the final approval date meet the eligibility criteria.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'used a mobile device running the Android operating system with a cellular data plan to access the internet since Nov. 12, 2017.' R2: 'Have used an Android device with a cellular data plan Accessed the internet... from Nov. 12, 2017, to the final approval.'
verifications.reasoning: References precisely match the eligibility criteria, including U.S. residents, Android device, cellular data plan, internet access, date range to final approval.

verifications.claim: No claim form is required for automatic payment if you received a notice.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'No claim form is required to benefit from the settlement. Class members who do not exclude themselves will automatically receive settlement benefits.' R6: 'There is no traditional claim form required... failing to choose a payment option could mean missing the payout if automatic delivery attempts fail.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references confirm no claim form needed; automatic benefits for non-excluded members, with notice implying selection for payment method.

verifications.claim: FederalCellularClassAction.com is the site to select a preferred payment method (PayPal, Zelle, etc.).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'visit the official website, FederalCellularClassAction.com, to choose how you want to be paid.' R6: 'official settlement website, FederalCellularClassAction.com... services like Zelle, PayPal or Venmo.' R1: 'select their preferred payment method on the settlement website... Federal Cellular Class Action.'
verifications.reasoning: References directly name the site and purpose for selecting payment methods including PayPal/Zelle.

verifications.claim: The final approval hearing is June 23, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The final approval hearing for the Google settlement is scheduled for June 23, 2026.' R2: 'A final approval hearing is scheduled for June 23, 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: All mentioning references unanimously state June 23, 2026, as the final approval hearing date.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The deadline for exclusion and objection to the class action settlement is May 29, 2026.' R2: 'The deadline to object to the settlement or opt out... is May 29, 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: References consistently list May 29, 2026, as opt-out/exclusion/objection deadline (R1 template mentions 05/09 elsewhere but main text confirms May 29).

verifications.claim: The lawsuit is Taylor v. Google LLC.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Taylor, et al. v. Google LLC, Case No. 5:20-cv-07956-VKD.' R2: 'Joseph Taylor, et al., v. Google LLC.'
verifications.reasoning: References directly name the lawsuit as Taylor v. Google LLC.

verifications.claim: Taylor v. Google LLC claimed that Android devices were programmed to transfer information to Google in the background even when not actively in use, consuming personal cellular data.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Google’s Android operating system caused devices to transfer information to Google without user permission. The transfers allegedly took place in the background, even when devices were idle and not in use.' R2: 'Android devices to send information back to its servers without user permission... even when the phones were sitting idle.'
verifications.reasoning: References describe the lawsuit claims matching exactly: background transfers on idle Android devices consuming cellular data.
